newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude prices weaker, Tapis premium tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude prices weaker, Tapis premium tumbles.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Monday, with indications of much lower Tapis premiums.
Brent and Dubai spreads were mostly steady, with Dubai looking to India's March tender for further price indications.
However, they said most Dubai appeared placed for March which might prompt India to fill in with West African or Gulf of Suez blend. Only one cargo and a partial were said available.
The tender closes on Thursday and is valid for one day.
One Lower Zakum deal was said done at ADNOC +25 cents, down from last week's deals at +30 cents. However, the deal may have been done last week, traders said.
A Lower Zakum at +20 cents from a shosha to a major was denied by the major.
A major sold Feb 8-10 Tapis at quoted plus 87 cents on Friday, cutting the previous premium of $1.75 dramatically.
Refinery margins on Tapis have been one of the worst hit. The major was said to be showing a second cargo for second half February in the market.
A producer said it was targeting early March premiums on Tapis at $1.45.
A major said a premium of $1.20 would be reasonable for March.
Australian availabilities were said to be tight with Kutubu sold out and only one or two Cossack and Griffin available.
But at the same time, traders said some West African imports were due in March and refinery margins were under pressure which could prompt cuts.

Minas premiums looked vulnerable on arbitrage barrels from West Africa because of a wide Minas/Brent spread. One trader said a shosha was offering February Minas at ICP +70 cents, but this could not be confirmed.
